g1.label: Greeting: ___ Dr Hall,
g1.why: Dear is the neutral greeting for a lecturer; Hey and Yo are too informal.

g2.label: I am writing ___ you about…
g2.why: Use to + infinitive to give the reason for writing: I am writing to ask.

g3.label: Could you ___ me how…
g3.why: Tell takes a person directly (tell me). We do not say say me or explain me.

g4.label: I was wondering ___ you could…
g4.why: I was wondering if + a past form is a soft, polite way to ask.

g5.label: Would it be possible ___ on Thursday?
g5.why: Would it be possible + to + infinitive is a polite request.

g6.label: Thank you ___ advance.
g6.why: The fixed phrase is thank you in advance.

g7.correct: Would it be possible to put up a sign about noise on the second floor?
accept: Would it be possible to put up a sign about noise on the second floor?
g7.label: 7. To the library office, about noise
g7.why: It is polite and clear. The others are an order and a very stiff demand.

g8.correct: Could I possibly have until Friday to hand in the task?
accept: Could I possibly have until Friday to hand in the task?
g8.label: 8. To a lecturer, about a deadline
g8.why: Could I possibly… softens the request. The others are an order and old-fashioned wording.

g9.correct: The heating has stopped working. I would be grateful if you could send someone to look at it.
accept: The heating has stopped working. I would be grateful if you could send someone to look at it.
g9.label: 9. To a landlord, about the heating
g9.why: It states the problem neutrally and makes a polite request. The others are rude or far too formal.

g10.correct: Could you tell me how the cafeteria decides how much food to prepare?
accept: Could you tell me how the cafeteria decides how much food to prepare?
g10.label: 10. To the cafeteria office, about waste
g10.why: A polite question with could you. The others accuse or sound like a legal demand.

g11.correct: I am writing to follow up on my email from Monday. I would appreciate a reply when you have time.
accept: I am writing to follow up on my email from Monday. I would appreciate a reply when you have time.
g11.label: 11. A reminder to a lecturer
g11.why: It refers to the earlier email and asks politely. The others sound rude or too stiff.

g12.label: 12. The ending of an email to a landlord
g12.why: Kind regards is the neutral closing. Cheers is too casual and the other is far too formal.
